notes: The cleft frame *it is* joins the participial predicate with the construction-supplied copula (rules 20 and 21), the explicit `הוּא` keeping only its own *he* and the substantival article only the relative *that* (rule 41).

*as at* is read as one compound rendering of `כְּ` headed on *as*: the subtraction test leaves no morpheme short of a rendering of its own, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met. The competing reading leaves *at* `added`, and it is named in that unit's note.
The assimilated article and the agreement article of ka-yyom ha-zzeh are both unrepresented, the phrase's one determiner being the demonstrative (rules 41 and 47).
